audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for sending the seventy-two, peace/hospitality, woes, return joy, revelation to infants, Good Samaritan, and Mary/Martha.

verses.restored: After these things the Lord appointed seventy-two others and sent them two by two before his face into every city and place where he himself was about to go.

familiar.text: After these things the LORD appointed other seventy also, and sent them two and two before his face into every city and place, whither he himself would come.

verses.restored: He said to them, The harvest is much, but the workers are few; therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.

familiar.text: Therefore said he unto them, The harvest truly is great, but the labourers are few: pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he would send forth labourers into his harvest.

verses.restored: Go; look, I send you as lambs in the middle of wolves.

familiar.text: Go your ways: behold, I send you forth as lambs among wolves.

verses.restored: Carry no purse, no bag, no sandals, and greet no one on the way.

familiar.text: Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor shoes: and salute no man by the way.

verses.restored: Whatever house you enter, first say, Peace to this house.

familiar.text: And into whatsoever house ye enter, first say, Peace be to this house.

verses.restored: If a child of peace is there, your peace will rest upon that one; if not, it will return to you.

familiar.text: And if the son of peace be there, your peace shall rest upon it: if not, it shall turn to you again.

verses.restored: Remain in the same house, eating and drinking what they provide, for the worker is worthy of wages. Do not move from house to house.

familiar.text: And in the same house remain, eating and drinking such things as they give: for the labourer is worthy of his hire. Go not from house to house.

verses.restored: Whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat what is set before you.

familiar.text: And into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you, eat such things as are set before you:

verses.restored: Heal the sick in it and say to them, The reign of the Divine has drawn near to you.

familiar.text: And heal the sick that are therein, and say unto them, The kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.

verses.restored: Whatever city you enter and they do not receive you, go out into its streets and say,

familiar.text: But into whatsoever city ye enter, and they receive you not, go your ways out into the streets of the same, and say,

verses.restored: Even the dust of your city that clings to our feet we wipe off against you; nevertheless know this: the reign of the Divine has drawn near.

familiar.text: Even the very dust of your city, which cleaveth on us, we do wipe off against you: notwithstanding be ye sure of this, that the kingdom of God is come nigh unto you.

verses.restored: I say to you, it will be more tolerable in that day for Sodom than for that city.

familiar.text: But I say unto you, that it shall be more tolerable in that day for Sodom, than for that city.

verses.restored: Woe to you, Chorazin; woe to you, Bethsaida. For if the powers done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have turned/realigned long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

familiar.text: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon, which have been done in you, they had a great while ago repented, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.

verses.restored: But it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon in the judgment than for you.

familiar.text: But it shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, than for you.

verses.restored: And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? You will be brought down to Hades/depths.

familiar.text: And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to heaven, shalt be thrust down to hell.

verses.restored: The one hearing you hears me; the one rejecting you rejects me; and the one rejecting me rejects the One who sent me.

familiar.text: He that heareth you heareth me; and he that despiseth you despiseth me; and he that despiseth me despiseth him that sent me.

verses.restored: The seventy-two returned with joy, saying, Lord, even the unclean spirits are subject to us in your name.

familiar.text: And the seventy returned again with joy, saying, Lord, even the devils are subject unto us through thy name.

verses.restored: He said to them, I was watching the Adversary fall from heaven like lightning.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.

verses.restored: Look, I have given you authority to tread on serpents and scorpions and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing will harm you.

familiar.text: Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.

verses.restored: Nevertheless, do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you; rejoice that your names have been written in the heavens.

familiar.text: Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven.

verses.restored: In that same hour he rejoiced in the holy Spirit and said, I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you hid these things from wise and understanding ones and revealed them to infants. Yes, Father, because this was pleasing before you.

familiar.text: In that hour Jesus rejoiced in spirit, and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes: even so, Father; for so it seemed good in thy sight.

verses.restored: All things were handed over to me by my Father; no one knows who the Son is except the Father, and who the Father is except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.

familiar.text: All things are delivered to me of my Father: and no man knoweth who the Son is, but the Father; and who the Father is, but the Son, and he to whom the Son will reveal him.

verses.restored: Turning to the disciples privately, he said, Blessed/flourishing are the eyes seeing what you see.

familiar.text: And he turned him unto his disciples, and said privately, Blessed are the eyes which see the things that ye see:

verses.restored: For I say to you that many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.

familiar.text: For I tell you, that many prophets and kings have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.

verses.restored: Look, a certain lawyer stood up to test him, saying, Teacher, what shall I do to inherit age-long life?

familiar.text: And, behold, a certain lawyer stood up, and tempted him, saying, Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?

verses.restored: He said to him, What has been written in the Law? How do you read?

familiar.text: He said unto him, What is written in the law? how readest thou?

verses.restored: He answered, You shall love the Lord your Divine from all your heart, all your soul/life, all your strength, and all your mind, and your neighbor as yourself.

familiar.text: And he answering said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, and with all thy mind; and thy neighbour as thyself.

verses.restored: He said to him, You answered rightly; do this, and you will live.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, Thou hast answered right: this do, and thou shalt live.

verses.restored: But he, wanting to justify himself, said to Jesus, And who is my neighbor?

familiar.text: But he, willing to justify himself, said unto Jesus, And who is my neighbour?

verses.restored: Jesus answered, A certain person was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers, who stripped him, beat him, and went away, leaving him half-dead.

familiar.text: And Jesus answering said, A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead.

verses.restored: By chance a certain priest was going down that way, and seeing him, passed by on the opposite side.

familiar.text: And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side.

verses.restored: Likewise also a Levite, coming to the place and seeing, passed by on the opposite side.

familiar.text: And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side.

verses.restored: But a certain Samaritan traveling came near him, and seeing him, was moved with compassion in the inward parts.

familiar.text: But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him,

verses.restored: Approaching, he bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine; placing him on his own animal, he brought him to an inn and cared for him.

familiar.text: And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

verses.restored: On the next day, taking out two denarii, he gave them to the innkeeper and said, Care for him; whatever more you spend, I will repay you when I return.

familiar.text: And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee.

verses.restored: Which of these three seems to you to have become neighbor to the one who fell among robbers?

familiar.text: Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves?

verses.restored: He said, The one who did mercy with him. Jesus said to him, Go, and you do likewise.

familiar.text: And he said, He that shewed mercy on him. Then said Jesus unto him, Go, and do thou likewise.

verses.restored: As they traveled, he entered a certain village. A woman named Martha welcomed him into her house.

familiar.text: Now it came to pass, as they went, that he entered into a certain village: and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.

verses.restored: She had a sister called Mary, who also sat at the Lord's feet and was hearing his word.

familiar.text: And she had a sister called Mary, which also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word.

verses.restored: Martha was distracted with much service. Standing near, she said, Lord, does it not matter to you that my sister left me to serve alone? Tell her then to help me.

familiar.text: But Martha was cumbered about much serving, and came to him, and said, Lord, dost thou not care that my sister hath left me to serve alone? bid her therefore that she help me.

verses.restored: The Lord answered her, Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things.

familiar.text: And Jesus answered and said unto her, Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things:

verses.restored: But one thing is necessary; Mary has chosen the beautiful/good portion, which will not be taken away from her.

familiar.text: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
